summary: Geshe Yeshe Tobden worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Geshe Lharampa at Sera Monastery (~1939–1959), studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1971).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa (~1899–1903). At Otani University, he served as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925), and he founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Gherardo Gnoli was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies who studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1954–1958). He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and served as president of ISMEO and IsIAO.

Ghulam Yazdani worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a B.A. from Aligarh Muslim University (~1903–1905). He was a professor at St. Stephen's College (1907), Rajshahi College (1909), and Government College University, Lahore (1913), before directing Hyderabad State's Archaeological Department (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981) and Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985) under Raniero Gnoli. She began teaching at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" around 1999.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Kyoto University (~1911–1914). He served as lecturer (1929) and associate professor (1935–1948) at Kyoto University, professor at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College, and director of Indo Bunka Kenkyujo.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, later serving there as assistant (1940), lecturer (1947), and professor (1968–1972), followed by a professorship at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal works in Buddhist studies, having earned a PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among other teachers. He taught at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and worked at the Insight Meditation Center (~2001).

Gilles Tarabout works in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Madeleine Biardeau. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at CNRS, a member of EHESS, and director of the Indo-French social sciences exchange program at FMSH.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the supervision of Jing Yin, also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Giovanni Gentile was a philosopher who studied at Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the universities of Pisa and Florence. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Sapienza, directed the Scuola Normale Superiore, and founded and presided over the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (1933).

Giovanni Vacca was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence. He taught Chinese at the University of Florence (1910) and held posts at Sapienza University of Rome from 1911 to 1948, including chair for History and Geography of East Asia.

Giovanni Verardi specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, having studied at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities. His posts include fellow at Ca' Foscari (1972–1987), reader at Bologna (1981–1987), and professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency University, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

Gisela Emma Full works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster, and was attested in 2013 as a research fellow at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisho Nakano was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate at Kyushu University. He held professorships at Peking University and Koyasan University, serving as Koyasan's president in 1951 and 1964.
Giti Dutt is a PhD student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.
